claims.text: Adding 5–10 vol% SiC nanoparticles to ZrB2 will act as a sintering aid.
The SiC-modified ZrB2 can be prepared at 2000–2200 °C with a holding time of 1–2 hours and pressure of 20–50 MPa.
SiC nanoparticles will form a liquid phase at lower preparation temperatures.
The proposed liquid phase will enhance diffusion in the ZrB2 material.
Adding SiC nanoparticles will lower the required preparation temperature relative to conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
SiC addition will increase density relative to conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
SiC addition will reduce porosity, holes, and defects relative to conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
SiC addition will enhance strength relative to conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
SiC addition will improve structural integrity after prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
SiC addition will reduce the component failure rate by 20–30% after prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly described as single-phase ZrB2 even after adding 5–10 vol% SiC. Retaining SiC as a distinct constituent would make the tested material a ZrB2–SiC multiphase composite rather than single-phase ZrB2.
